record.paper_title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Suppose the regular Lagrangian flow X(t,x) of a Sobolev vector field admits a first-order expansion in the differentiability-in-measure sense, so that for small r one has X(t, x + r y) = X(t, x) + r A(t, x) y plus an error that tends to 0 locally in measure. What is the nature of the matrix-valued map A(t,x) that appears in this expansion?

evidence.quote: This result raises in a natural way the following questions: What is the nature of A?
in turn, differentiability in measure is equivalent to |f(x+ry)-f(x)-rA(x)y|/r -> 0 locally in measure as r downarrow 0, for all y in R^n, for some matrix-valued local map A(x).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $b:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a Sobolev vector field (with bounded divergence) and let $X(t,x)$ denote its associated regular Lagrangian flow, i.e., the unique (up to Lebesgue-negligible sets) Borel map satisfying $\partial_t X(t,x)=b(t,X(t,x))$ with $X(0,x)=x$ and the bounded compressibility condition $X(t,\cdot)_\#\mathcal{L}^n\le C\,\mathcal{L}^n$.

Recall that a Borel map $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m$ is said to be differentiable in measure at $x$ with derivative the matrix $A(x)$ if, for every $y\in\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$\frac{|f(x+ry)-f(x)-rA(x)y|}{r}\xrightarrow[r\downarrow 0]{}0\quad\text{locally in measure.}$$

Suppose that for each $t\in[0,T]$ the map $x\mapsto X(t,x)$ is differentiable in measure, so that there exists a matrix-valued Borel map $A(t,x)\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ with
$$X(t,x+ry)=X(t,x)+r\,A(t,x)\,y+o(r)\qquad\text{locally in measure as }r\downarrow 0,\;\forall y\in\mathbb{R}^n.$$

Determine the nature of the matrix-valued map $A(t,x)$: identify a canonical equation it must satisfy (for instance, an ODE along trajectories of the form $\frac{d}{dt}A(t,x)=M(t,X(t,x))\,A(t,x)$ for an appropriate matrix field $M$ derived from the distributional derivative $Db$, together with $A(0,x)=I$), and characterize its regularity.
artifact.category_tag: Regular Lagrangian flows of weakly differentiable vector fields
artifact.status_search_result: For Sobolev vector fields, Ambrosio–Malý and subsequent works established that the flow is differentiable in measure and that the derivative matrix $W(t,x)$ satisfies an ODE driven by the disintegration of $Db$ along the flow with $W(0,x)=I$. The corresponding question for BV (and nearly incompressible BV) vector fields has been partially addressed in more recent work (e.g., Bianchini–Bonicatto, ARMA 2022) and remains an active area, so the matter is partially solved in general.

status_evidence.title: Differentiability in Measure of the Flow Associated with a Nearly Incompressible BV Vector Field
status_evidence.snippet: The flow is differentiable in measure in the sense of Ambrosio–Malý, with derivative W(t,y) satisfying an ODE involving the disintegration of the distributional derivative of the vector field.
status_evidence.claim: Identifies the nature of the derivative matrix as a solution to a linear ODE along the flow driven by Db, partially answering the question in the BV setting.

status_evidence.title: Differentiability properties of the flow of 2d autonomous vector fields
status_evidence.snippet: Studies under which assumptions the flow associated to autonomous planar vector fields inherits Sobolev/BV regularity.
status_evidence.claim: Active investigation of regularity of A(t,x) in low-dimensional cases.
